question: Has anyone in board gaming ever run app sponsorships or partnerships, and what did they actually look like?
note_on_rates: Every figure below is an ADVERTISED or CLAIMED rate, not a transaction price. Board gaming ad slots are sold by individuals and small teams and are routinely discounted, bartered, or comped. SponsorRadar figures are algorithmic estimates produced by a third-party tool from public video metadata, not disclosed deal values.

app_publisher_partnerships.case: Dized (interactive rules/tutorial app) partnering with publishers
app_publisher_partnerships.shape: App builds official interactive tutorials and living rules for the publisher's games; publisher tools let companies create their own rules/FAQ content
app_publisher_partnerships.date: publisher tools and partnerships announced from 2018 onward

app_publisher_partnerships.case: Gloomhaven Helper (third-party companion app) and Cephalofair Games
app_publisher_partnerships.shape: Esoteric Software built Gloomhaven Helper on a non-commercial basis under an implied licence from the publisher. When the developer began charging for some versions, the publisher considered the implied licence broken; the developer ceased development and the app was withdrawn. Cephalofair then partnered with digital studio Lucky Duck Games for official Gloomhaven and Frosthaven companion apps.
app_publisher_partnerships.outcome_for_indie_dev: app removed; replaced by publisher-chosen studio; community forks (Gloomhaven Secretariat, X-haven Assistant) filled the gap
app_publisher_partnerships.note: Kickstarter update page returned HTTP 403 to automated fetching; details taken from trade coverage and search summaries.

app_publisher_partnerships.case: Board Game Stats (BG Stats) and BoardGameGeek
app_publisher_partnerships.shape: Paid third-party app syncs collections and posts plays to BGG using the user's own BGG credentials, and imports plays from BGG, Yucata and Board Game Arena. Neither the app's site nor its FAQ mentions any partnership, licence or permission from BGG.

affiliate_arrangements.detail: Commission on iOS and Mac apps and in-app content removed from Apple's affiliate programme effective 2018-10-01 (rate had already been cut from 7% to 2.5% in April 2017). The successor Apple Services Performance Partners programme covers Apple Music, Apple TV, Apple Podcasts memberships and sales of movies, TV, books and audiobooks - not app downloads or IAP.

where_i_looked_and_found_nothing: BGG advertising rate card (archived): no app/digital/software advertiser category; all seven published testimonials are physical-game publishers
BGG affiliate programme: explicitly scoped to retailers
Meeple Mountain partner page: 60+ named clients, no apps or digital products mentioned
Board Game Quest review service: review scope limited to "games that have been published and are currently available for retail sale"
The Game Crafter's list of 11 recommended board game reviewers: no fees published, no mention of apps
Dice Tower 'What's APPening': 20+ recent episodes, no sponsorship labels, no utility/companion apps covered
Dice Tower West exhibitor and sponsor material: no software or app companies identified
Searches for sponsor reads naming a tabletop tracker, scorekeeper or companion app on any board game channel, podcast or newsletter: nothing found
Searches for 'sponsored by Board Game Arena', Gamefound, BackerKit, Dized or Tabletop Simulator on board game podcasts: nothing verifiable found; only organic/editorial coverage
BoardGameWire sponsored-content tag: only one sponsored article surfaced (Boardssey, B2B)
